2609.25186.title: From Pattern Recognizers to Personalized Companions: A Survey of Large Language Models in Mental Health
2609.25186.paper_summary: The rising global prevalence of mental health conditions, together with longstanding barriers in traditional healthcare, such as limited resources, high cost, stigma, and privacy concerns, has created an urgent need for accessible and scalable support. Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a transformative technology with strong potential to democratize mental health support through advanced natural language understanding and generation. However, the rapidly expanding, fragmented body of work in this area lacks a coherent evolutionary narrative, making it difficult to contextualize current progress and identify future directions. This survey addresses this gap by organizing and analyzing the literature around a central thesis: the role of LLMs in mental health is evolving through three distinct, increasingly sophisticated phases. We trace this trajectory from Phase I, in which LLMs act primarily as passive Information Tools and Pattern Recognizers for assessment; through Phase II, where they function as Empathetic Conversationalists for in-the-moment, stateless interactions; to the current frontier, Phase III, which seeks Longitudinal, Personalized Companions implemented as stateful cognitive agents. To support this framework, we systematically review core technologies, agent architectures (Profile, Memory, Reasoning, and Planning), and the critical infrastructure of datasets and benchmarks, highlighting how their evolution underpins this developmental path. Viewing the field through this developmental lens, we provide a comprehensive synthesis of existing work, an insightful narrative of its trajectory, and a clear roadmap for future innovation in responsible, effective, and human-centered AI for mental healthcare. A curated collection of the resources reviewed in this survey is available at our project repository: https://github.com/Emo-gml/Awesome-Mental-Health-LLMs.
2609.25186.paper_summary_zh: 全球心理健康狀況的上升流行率，加上傳統醫療中長期存在的障礙，如資源有限、高成本、污名化和隱私問題，創造了對可獲得和可擴展支持的迫切需求。大型語言模型（LLMs）已經成為一種變革性技術，具有通過先進的自然語言理解和生成來民主化心理健康支持的強大潛力。然而，這一領域快速擴展且支離破碎的研究體系缺乏一致的演變敘事，這使得難以將當前的進展置於上下文中並確定未來的方向。本調查通過圍繞一個中心論題組織和分析文獻，填補了這一空白：LLMs在心理健康中的角色正通過三個明確且日益精緻的階段演變。我們追溯這一軌跡，從第一階段，在這一階段中，LLMs主要作為被動的信息工具和模式識別器進行評估；到第二階段，它們作為同理心的對話者進行即時的無狀態互動；再到當前的前沿，第三階段，尋求作為有狀態的認知代理實現的縱向個性化伴侶。為了支持這一框架，我們系統性地回顧了核心技術、代理架構（配置、記憶、推理和規劃）以及數據集和基準的關鍵基礎設施，突顯了它們的演變如何支撐這一發展路徑。通過這一發展視角來看待該領域，我們提供了現有工作的全面綜合、其軌跡的深刻敘事，以及未來在負責任、有效和以人為中心的心理健康護理AI中的創新清晰路線圖。本調查中回顧的資源的策劃集合可在我們的項目庫中獲得：https://github.com/Emo-gml/Awesome-Mental-Health-LLMs。
